newsitem.title: USA: BellSouth access lines up 4.7 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: BellSouth access lines up 4.7 pct in 1996.

text.p: BellSouth Corp on Thursday said its access lines grew 4.7 percent in 1996, adding just over one million lines, the first regional Bell to do so. Its total lines to customers grew to 22.1 million.
Business access lines increased by 8.1 percent in the year.
Revenue from calling features like caller ID, voice mail and voice dialling grew rapidly to account for $1 billion in annual revenue in 1996. No year ago figure was given.
BellSouth's fourth quarter earnings per share before one-time items were $0.64 per share, a cent above analysts consensus on First Call, and 12.3 percent above the $0.57 of a year ago.
Including year ago special charges of $0.73 per share, the company made a loss of $0.16 in the fourth quarter of 1995.

BellSouth's U.S. cellular customers jumped 26.9 percent in 1996 to 3.61 million but average revenue per customer slipped to $56 from $61. During the fourth quarter the company added 279,000 U.S. cellular customers and 765,000 for the year.

The company had an 8.88 percent cellular market penetration compared with 7.13 percent a year ago. This is the proportion of people who live in its licenses areas that use the company's cellular services.

"We're in an industry that's on fast forward," said Duane Ackerman, BellSouth chief executive with reference to the telecommunications industry. "The result of this (BellSouth) market focus is steady earnings growth," he said.

Total operating revenues rose six percent to $5.05 billion from $4.76 billion in the fourth quarter and operating expenses rose 5.7 percent, excluding special charges in the year ago quarter for workforce reductions.
Telephone operations cash expenses rose 0.7 percent in the fourth quarter from a year ago.
The stock closed 1-1/2 lower at 42-3/8 as the broad market fell. (( Nick Louth, New York Newsroom 212 859 1712))
